title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a duck in Austin, Texas while in autonomous mode. The vehicle did not slow down or stop, and the incident occurred near Mueller Lake where the duck had become known to neighbors. This shows a failure in object detection or collision avoidance, where the system either did not identify the animal in its path or did not execute a stopping response.

The failure happened in a live deployment on public streets, where these decisions occur without human intervention. It would have taken either better training of the perception model to detect small animals, or an abundance-of-caution design that treats ambiguous moving objects as obstacles requiring defensive action, to prevent this outcome.

It is not established whether the vehicle's behavior represented a flaw in the technology, whether improved detection would have been feasible given the circumstances, or what specific design trade-offs Avride considered in its response.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, causing significant community concern about self-driving car technology. The incident gained attention after a resident posted about the vehicle hitting the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck, which had been nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant, had become familiar to neighbors, intensifying their outrage. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode at the time of the incident. While the company investigated claims that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign and found no supporting evidence, it has adjusted operations by excluding certain streets near the lake from its testing area. Avride is now conducting simulations to evaluate potential technological improvements to prevent similar situations while ensuring changes do not compromise overall safety performance.
